stories.primary_headline: Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province in DR Congo, death toll tops 4,500

primary_source.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province in DR Congo, death toll tops 4,500
primary_source.content: The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.The emergence of cases in the province, which borders Central African Republic, poses a new challenge for health authorities struggling to contain the outbreak.The National Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed two cases - including one death - in North Ubangi.Reuters reported on Thursday that two cases were confirmed in the province, citing two health officials. At the time, there was no official statement by Congolese authorities.WHO says Congo Ebola outbreak can still be brought under control within three monthsNorth Ubangi becomes the eighth province affected by the outbreak, alongside North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Kivu, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi.The outbreak, the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo's history, has already spread beyond the country's borders, with cases recorded in Uganda and seven infections confirmed in Kenya this month.Congo's latest situation report showed 67 new confirmed cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to Oct.16, bringing the cumulative total to 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began.The outbreak remains concentrated in eastern Congo, with Ituri province reporting 44 of the 67 new cases.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Keep away from the doctor’: a visit to an influencer’s wellness event, where the advice could kill

primary_source.headline: ‘Keep away from the doctor’: a visit to an influencer’s wellness event, where the advice could kill
primary_source.content: Barbara O’Neill, identified as a risk to public safety in Australia, dismisses antibiotics, vaccines and scientifically proven cancer treatment at UK conferenceA roar of laughter erupts from a crowd inside a large conference room at the De Vere Cranage Estate hotel. The joke? The idea that visiting the doctor could help treat a serious illness.On stage the controversial Australian proponent of natural remedies Barbara O’Neill is taking part in a question-and-answer session during a five-day wellness conference, where science mixes uncomfortably with Bible verse and potentially deadly pseudo-scientific practices. Continue reading...
